templates.title: Family change
templates.description: A new family member, a marriage or a family member arriving in Canada.

tasks.title: Add the family member to your SettleWise household
Apply for provincial health coverage for the family member
Apply for the Canada Child Benefit
Register children for school or childcare
Update insurance policies and beneficiaries
Speak with a licensed professional before any sponsorship application
tasks.guidance: SettleWise does not give immigration advice. A licensed consultant or lawyer can review your situation.

tasks.title: Update your household budget

templates.title: Moving home
templates.description: Plan a move - notice, lease, utilities, insurance, address changes and costs.

tasks.title: Give written notice to your current landlord
tasks.guidance: Check your lease and provincial rules for how much notice is required and how it must be given.

tasks.title: Sign the new lease and keep a copy
tasks.guidance: Read the lease before signing. Keep a copy with your documents.

tasks.title: Book movers or a truck rental
tasks.guidance: Get at least two quotes. Confirm the date, insurance and what is included.

tasks.title: Confirm tenant insurance starts on the move date
tasks.guidance: Many landlords ask for proof of tenant insurance before you get the keys.

tasks.title: Schedule hydro, gas and internet transfer
tasks.guidance: Ask each provider to stop service at the old address and start it at the new one on the move date.

tasks.title: Register children at the new school
Set up mail forwarding
Update your address with the CRA
Update your address with IRCC
Update the address on your health card and driver's licence
Update the address on your vehicle permit
Update your address with your bank and other insurers

templates.title: Starting a new job
templates.description: Payroll, banking, tax forms, benefits and commute for a new position.

tasks.title: Have your Social Insurance Number ready for your employer
Read the basics of employment standards in your province
Plan your commute and buy a transit pass if needed
Complete your federal and provincial TD1 forms
Give your employer direct deposit details
Enrol in workplace benefits before the deadline
Add your new income to your budget

templates.title: Permanent residence preparation
templates.description: Organise documents and timelines before a permanent residence application.

tasks.title: Read the official program guide and document checklist
Book an approved language test
Book a consultation with a licensed professional for case-specific questions
tasks.guidance: SettleWise organises your documents and dates; it does not assess eligibility.

tasks.title: Request police certificates from each country you lived in
Gather identity and civil status documents for each family member
Get certified translations of documents not in English or French
Prepare proof of funds statements
Get photos that meet the specifications

templates.title: International travel
templates.description: Travel outside Canada and come back without document surprises.

tasks.title: Check your passport is valid for the whole trip
Check your PR card is valid for your return date
Count your days in Canada for the residency obligation
Apply for a PR travel document if your card will expire abroad
Book flights
Buy travel medical insurance for your dates
Check travel advice for your destination
Tell your bank and card issuer about your travel dates

sources.title: New immigrants - IRCC
sources.summary: Starting point for people who recently immigrated: what to do after arriving, getting important documents, finding free settlement services and keeping IRCC informed of changes such as a new address.

sources.title: PR card - IRCC
sources.summary: How to apply for, renew or replace a permanent resident card. Permanent residents need a valid PR card or a PR travel document to board a flight back to Canada.

sources.title: Understand permanent resident status - IRCC
sources.summary: Explains the rights of permanent residents and the residency obligation: permanent residents must be physically present in Canada for a minimum number of days within a five-year period.

sources.title: Permanent resident travel document - IRCC
sources.summary: Permanent residents outside Canada without a valid PR card can apply for a permanent resident travel document (PRTD) to return to Canada by plane, train, bus or boat.

sources.title: Immigrate to Canada - IRCC
sources.summary: Overview of immigration programs and links to each program's official guide and document checklist. Program rules and eligibility are set by IRCC.

sources.title: Canadian citizenship eligibility - IRCC
sources.summary: Official requirements to become a Canadian citizen, including physical presence, tax filing and language requirements, with a presence calculator.

sources.title: Find free newcomer services near you - IRCC
sources.summary: Search tool for free, government-funded newcomer services such as settlement help, language classes and job search support, by postal code.

sources.title: Find a licensed immigration consultant - College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants
sources.publisher: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants
sources.summary: The regulator for immigration and citizenship consultants in Canada. Use its public register to check that a consultant is licensed before paying for advice.

sources.title: Social Insurance Number - Service Canada
sources.summary: You need a Social Insurance Number to work in Canada or receive government benefits. Explains who can apply, the documents needed and how to keep your SIN protected.

sources.title: Newcomers to Canada (immigrants) - CRA
sources.summary: Tax information for newcomers: residency status for tax purposes, filing your first return and applying for benefits and credits.

sources.title: My Account for individuals - CRA
sources.summary: The CRA's secure online portal. You can view tax and benefit information and change your address after you move.

sources.title: TD1 Personal Tax Credits Returns - CRA
sources.summary: Federal and provincial TD1 forms you give a new employer so they deduct the right amount of income tax from your pay.

sources.title: Canada Child Benefit - CRA
sources.summary: A tax-free monthly payment to eligible families to help with the cost of raising children under 18. Explains who can apply and how.

sources.title: Apply for OHIP and get a health card - Ontario
sources.summary: How to apply for Ontario Health Insurance Plan coverage and a health card, who is eligible and the documents to bring to ServiceOntario.

sources.title: Change your address - Ontario
sources.summary: Change the address on your Ontario driver's licence, vehicle permit and health card, online or in person at ServiceOntario.

sources.title: Renting in Ontario - your rights
sources.summary: Rights and responsibilities of tenants and landlords in Ontario, including the standard lease, rent deposits, rent increases and how to end a tenancy.

sources.title: Your guide to the Employment Standards Act - Ontario
sources.summary: Minimum standards for most workplaces in Ontario: pay, hours, overtime, vacation, public holidays and leaves.

sources.title: Mail forwarding - Canada Post
sources.summary: Forward your mail to a new address for a chosen period when you move. A fee applies.

sources.title: Opening a bank account - Financial Consumer Agency of Canada
sources.summary: Your rights when opening a bank account, the identification banks may accept and how to compare account fees.

sources.title: Travel advice and advisories - Government of Canada
sources.summary: Official travel advice for every country, entry requirements and what to know before you leave Canada.

sources.title: Job Bank - Government of Canada
sources.summary: Government job board with job postings, wage information and career planning tools.
